findings.criterion: real trio run returns a validated handback; malformed/incomplete still leaves something to read; campaign ledger is single source of truth
findings.message: D-A locks a decision *rule* before measurement, then forks product law into three incompatible regimes (refuse on absent soft fields / degrade / strike-or-amend) depending on an extractability matrix that does not yet exist. A future maintainer—and Stage-2—cannot know which envelope is the product. The success criteria still list six required fields as if the strict envelope is settled. Until Stage-1 lock records the measured branch with `who` and rewrites criteria 3 / Phase 8 to a single non-forked acceptance law, this is not a locked design; it is a choose-your-own-handback plan that will be “implemented” three different ways under schedule pressure.

findings.criterion: nothing spent, written, or started without human confirmation; single writer proven; honest Roadmap status
findings.message: Phase 1 is allowed to ship the full talk→artifact motion without concurrency/crash receipts, CAS/idempotency/auth baseline, lease liveness, or real-Crucible HALT—while insisting those gates are “named and owed.” The debt lives only in paragraph lists. There is no machine-checkable owed-gate register, no Phase-10 gate that fails if any Phase-1 skip lacks a later receipt, and no rule that a later wave may not declare GREEN while an owed gate is still open. A future maintainer cannot tell done from deferred; schedule pressure will treat Phase-1 GREEN as the product. For a plan whose North Star is “no silent spend + ledger truth,” unenforced debt is a silent-exemption machine.

findings.criterion: project stood up, planned, and driven by talking to its steward (compile Face/Roadmap, propose named-step commission, typed refine, start→Foreman)
findings.message: The North Star product is “the steward.” The draft never draws a maintainable boundary: which modules own dialogue compile, draft-Face, propose/confirm surface, adapter, handback, Roadmap projection, and AWAITING YOU. Work is scattered across job-lifecycle line cites, packet-view, store writers, supervisor, and unnamed UI. A future maintainer will not know where “talk to the steward” lives, will re-implement conversation and confirm paths in new call sites, and will re-open the multi-writer / multi-confirm bypasses Phase 0–3 try to close. Without a seam map and “one owner per motion,” the talk path is institutional knowledge, not a system.

findings.criterion: nothing starts or proceeds without human confirmation; Roadmap shows the truth about what is waiting/running; non-goal forbids changing trio sources
findings.message: Gate inventory is a one-time Phase-0 table (verbatim text + sha256). Pre-answering is hash-exact; unknown halts show raw text. The plan never says who re-runs the inventory when Crucible/Foreman change gate wording, resume flags, or blocker shapes on *their* cadence (allowed by non-goal: you do not control them). A future maintainer inherits a frozen inventory that silently drifts into “everything is unknown halt” or, worse, stale pre-answer opt-ins that no longer match live engines. Without a versioned re-inventory trigger (trio version / binary hash / inventory age) and a test that fails when live halt text is neither inventoried nor routed as unknown, confirmation and honest wait-state rot by default.

findings.criterion: confirmed commission executes as a real trio/Foreman run; Roadmap truth across halt/resume/restart
findings.message: Phase 5 makes `--resume` primary and live-stdin a “fallback if resume is measured lossy,” then Phase 7 builds budget-breach resume on the same fork (resume suspended job object vs relaunch `--resume`, with honesty text if lossy). The measurement is deferred into the build. That freezes two execution topologies as forever-supported unless a later decision kills one. A future maintainer debugging “confirm said continue but the run re-billed / lost checkpoint / wrong wave state” has no single resume law—only a matrix of job-object + checkpoint + optional stdin bridge. Lock one resume contract (or a dated kill of the other) before Phases 5/7 both harden both paths.

findings.criterion: Anchor executes a real trio run; when he says start, Foreman executes; Roadmap shows true state
findings.message: From Phase 1/4 onward, CI and continuous proof lean on a stub/rehearsal commission emitting canned doc-trio bytes. Real Crucible appears only as one observed HALT cycle (Phase 5); real Foreman only as one observed wave (Phase 9). There is no standing contract that rehearsal argv, halt shape, journal events, and handback extractors are re-diffed against live engines on a cadence. Future maintainers will keep green stub CI while the paid path drifts—exactly the failure mode that already burned auth-ON. A North Star that requires *real* execution needs a real-path canary that fails the suite when stub and live diverge, not a one-shot human observation per phase.

findings.criterion: steward proposes a commission for a named roadmap step (skill+seat+depth) without doing the planning itself
findings.message: The inverse guard depends on the proposer *declaring* whether it invented plan content. Models (and future prompt edits) will learn to under-report invention. That lets HOW leak into propose-time derivation while compile stays “WHAT/WHY-only,” violating the non-goal that the steward commissions rather than plans—and producing confidently wrong skill/seat/depth on the confirm screen. A future maintainer cannot audit the bright line without an external oracle (forbidden construct lint on propose inputs/outputs, fixture steps that must refuse, or human-labeled probe corpus). Self-attestation is not a maintainable guardrail.

findings.criterion: campaign ledger is single source of truth; Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.message: The plan admits the ledger *lags* between Python outbox append and Node drain, says the bound is “measured and recorded,” and forbids presenting undrained outbox as live status. It never defines an enforceable lag SLO, a surface that shows “as of seq N / lag exceeds bound,” or a failure when the drain stalls. A future maintainer inherits a system that can be “correct by design” while the Roadmap is minutes stale—or stuck—without failing any named gate. Honest status requires a numeric bound + test/alert, not a wave-receipt footnote.

findings.criterion: plan is an artifact John can change by talking; commissions pin Face hash; ledger remains SSOT
findings.message: Face versions are immutable and content-addressed; commissions pin Face hash; handbacks carry provenance. There is no migration/compat rule for when the Face step shape, draft-Face document, commission record, or handback envelope must change. A future maintainer either freezes schemas forever or ships breaking writers that leave old chain_id histories unreadable or unre-commissionable. Without versioned schemas + explicit read-compat tests (“old Face hash still resolves; old confirmation still reconstructs”), the ledger SSOT claim dies at the first enrichment the plan itself invites via “future decision-log entries.”

findings.criterion: full talk→Face→propose→confirm→run→artifact→honest status motion
findings.message: Phase 1 GREEN requires “one observed run of the full motion, by John, on the real machine.” That is a fine Stage-1 demo, not a maintainable regression gate. Future maintainers (and later waves) cannot re-prove the spine without the same human ritual, so the motion will silently regress between Phase 1 and Phase 10. Pair the human observation with an automatable auth-ON spine script that asserts the same chain_id-linked observables; otherwise the walking skeleton cannot walk after the author leaves the room.

findings.criterion: commission proposed and confirmed only through explicit human confirmation before spend
findings.message: The plan identifies the confirmation choke as `proposeCommission (141) / confirmCommission (250)`. Line numbers rot on the next edit; a future maintainer grepping the plan will trust the wrong symbols or invent a parallel entrypoint. Name stable module exports + a single-entrypoint invariant test (“all start paths call X”), not source coordinates.

findings.criterion: typed description produces Face/roadmap with zero chat turns persisted; ledger is Strip + roadmap events + Face narrative
findings.message: The plan allows structured append-only draft-Face state while banning dialogue turns, then defines the zero-chat proof as “scan every table/file/blob for any persisted dialogue turn.” It never defines the schema predicate that distinguishes allowed framing fields from forbidden transcript. A future maintainer will reintroduce near-transcript blobs under “structured state” and still pass a naive string scan—or fail the scan on legitimate draft text. Specify the allowed draft schema and scan against that whitelist.

findings.criterion: no bespoke plan template; Crucible plan shape IS the template; reviewable artifact on screen
findings.message: If classifyArtifact fails, the only non-amendment path is a “DOC-TRIO MANIFEST” that packages bytes the classifier already understands. “Packaging” is undefined (file layout? synthetic metadata? rewritten headings?). A future maintainer under delivery pressure will grow the manifest into a second plan shape while claiming non-goal compliance. Bound the manifest to an explicit, testable contract (list of allowed transforms; golden bytes; forbid new sections/fields not present on disk).

findings.criterion: nothing spent or decided without human confirmation (budget must not remove required confirms)
findings.message: “≤2 spend-confirms and ≤5 gate-confirms for stand-up-to-artifact” is asserted, not derived from the North Star’s required confirms (Face first write + three Crucible approvals + spend, etc.). The “one spare” is unexplained. A future maintainer will either treat the numbers as sacred UX law or quietly raise them. Tie the budget to a named enumerate of required confirms so breaches diagnose missing/extra gates rather than vibes.

findings.criterion: n/a
findings.section: Process / last revision metadata (not a plan phase)
findings.message: The reviser’s changelog is thirty identical “Applied a search/replace patch” lines. That does not refute a North Star criterion, but it does make future Shark/maintainer comparison of revisions impossible. Demote per inclusion test; fix process, not product scope.

findings.criterion: steward proposes a commission for a named roadmap step and only on confirmation Anchor executes it as a real trio run; the produced plan comes back as an artifact John can read
findings.message: Steel-man the premise that “the whole North Star is ONE motion” and that an early end-to-end slice can kill or reshape the spine. Even granted, Phase 1 stubs the only leg that makes the motion the North Star: the real trio. The slice proves typed describe → Face → propose → confirm → stub → canned doc-trio → card → status. That is orchestration plumbing. It cannot falsify whether a confirmed commission against real Crucible yields a plan John can read and correct by talking, nor whether “nothing is spent without confirmation” still holds when the engine actually spends. The named falsifiers are almost all about compile, confirm-count, classifier, or status-without-supervisor — none is “real commission failed to produce a reviewable plan.” A green Phase 1 therefore over-claims ordering evidence: it can kill talk-surface shape, not the commission→plan premise the North Star is about. Either Phase 1 must include one real (even single-gate) Crucible hop, or the plan must stop saying Phase 1 can kill the spine of the North Star motion.

findings.criterion: when he says start, Foreman executes and the Roadmap shows the truth about what is running; plan comes back as artifact; nothing spent/written/started without confirmation
findings.message: Steel-man the phased inversion: prove HALT first, Foreman last, then auth-ON acceptance. The product sentence in the North Star is one arc: talk → Face/roadmap → commission → real plan → read/correct by talk → say start → Foreman runs → Roadmap tells the truth. No phase’s GREEN condition is that full arc. Phase 5 greens on one halt→confirm→resume “to the next gate,” not Stage-2 plan on screen. Phase 9 greens on typed start → one Foreman wave → wave state across restart, assuming an already-approved plan. Phase 10 runs per-criterion scenarios (1–5 and 8) in isolation, not one observed stand-up-through-Foreman chain with ledger chain_id reconstruction of that full spend. Confirm-count is re-measured only for “stand-up-to-artifact,” not stand-up-to-Foreman-running. Even the strongest reading of “eight criteria cover the North Star” fails: the North Star is a single continuous behavior, and the plan never requires one green observation of that continuous behavior. Without that, the plan can ship eight green checkboxes and still never have demonstrated the product.

findings.criterion: produced plan comes back as an artifact John can read on screen; nothing is started without human confirmation
findings.message: Steel-man “HALT is the normal path; unattended completion is special.” Crucible’s design is three you-approve gates before a plan is an artifact. Proving one observed halt→ask→confirm→resume cycle only proves the resume channel for a single gate hop. It does not prove: durable halt records across three sequential gates, three gate-confirms each recording `who`, no silent auto-pass, and a final reviewable plan card. The negative test “zero confirmation records cannot reach Stage-2 output” is necessary but not sufficient as the phase GREEN — a run could still break on the second or third gate after Phase 5 is declared green. If HALT-first is the load-bearing inversion, GREEN must be the multi-gate path that actually yields the artifact the North Star promises, not “reaches the next gate.”

findings.criterion: NON-GOAL — nothing that makes the steward do the planning itself rather than commission it; steward compiles description into Face and Roadmap, then proposes a commission
findings.section: Phase 0 D-C / D-C inverse guard; Phase 6 proposability probe
findings.message: Steel-man D-C: compile emits only WHAT/WHY so the steward does not invent HOW; size/seat/depth appear only at propose-before-spend. The inverse guard then requires every step to be proposable (skill + seat + depth) from step text + Face alone, and on failure the compile must multi-turn ask John clarifying questions until proposability passes. That loop is interactive scoping and decomposition under a different name. It is not “commission planning” — it is the steward driving planning-quality content into the Face before any commission exists, exactly the non-goal the bright line claims to prevent. Steel-manning “clarifications are still WHAT/WHY” does not help: the North Star separates compile-from-description vs commission-a-named-step; an unbounded clarify-until-proposable dialogue is planning work performed by the steward. The plan needs a hard stop (max clarify turns, escalate to John choosing “commission research/framing” as an explicit step, or accept that some steps are not yet commissionable without calling that “planning”).

findings.criterion: campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.section: Phase 2 honest SSOT bound; Phase 4 lease liveness; Success criterion 5 and 7
findings.message: Steel-man the outbox design: Python cannot write roadmap_events; Node drains; at-least-once with dedupe; projection says “as of seq N.” The draft itself then makes liveness come from the lease, “never from the outbox,” and forbids presenting un-drained outbox as live status. That is two sources of truth by construction: ledger for committed history, lease for “is it running.” Criterion 7 (“roadmap_events has exactly ONE writer… campaign ledger SSOT”) and criterion 5 (“Roadmap reflects ACTUAL state”) are only jointly true if the plan names the dual model and defines which surface is authoritative for which question. As written, “single source of truth” is prose that the same phase falsifies. Steel-man cannot rescue a title claim the body retracts; rename SSOT to “append-only event log + lease-derived liveness” and make criterion 5/7 acceptance assert both, or the Roadmap can be “honest” while the ledger is stale and still called SSOT.

findings.criterion: real trio run returns a plan John can read; no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime; campaign ledger remains truth
findings.section: Phase 0 D-A and extractability matrix; Phase 8; Success criterion 3
findings.message: Steel-man “extract, do not invent” and the non-goal of zero trio source changes. D-A pre-commits refusal/degraded/strike rules to measured absent-rates on fields the trio was never designed to emit. If the matrix shows high absence (likely for uncertainty_flags, tool_depth_why, human_wait), criterion 3’s happy path — receipt-validate accepts a full envelope — becomes rare or impossible without amending the non-goal or striking fields. The degraded path (raw doc-trio + partial card + REFUSED banner) satisfies “never invisible spend” but does not satisfy “validated handback” or a trusted ledger receipt of what the run meant. The plan has no success bar for happy-path handback rate, no Stage-1 decision of which fields are load-bearing for “plan as artifact” vs Strip metadata, and Phase 10 still asserts “a real trio run returns a handback that receipt-validate.mjs accepts” as if that were independent of D-A’s measurement. Steel-manning extraction without a defined “good enough for North Star” envelope leaves criterion 3 either silently always-degraded or a future amendment bomb mid-build.

findings.criterion: campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; nothing spent/written/started without confirmation
findings.section: Phase 1 near-term specifics (real substrate, real writer)
findings.message: Steel-man “skeleton first so failure can still kill or reshape the spine.” Phase 1 already mandates D-B’s store (local non-synced SQLite/WAL), the single Node writer, roadmap_events/commissions/confirmations/blob shapes, real token/confirm grammar, and ledger events. The only allowed stub is the trio leg. The falsifiers reshape Phase 6 (compile line), Phases 3/7 (confirm budget), Phase 8 timing (artifact), or Phase 4 timing (lease) — not the outbox/single-writer/SQLite premise. So the “kill the spine” claim is oversold: the architectural spine is locked before it is stress-tested by real spend, real multi-gate HALT, or real Foreman. Ordering evidence is only about talk/confirm UX, while the durability and confirmation choke points the North Star depends on are already chosen. Either Phase 1 must be allowed to reject D-B/outbox on evidence, or the plan must stop claiming Phase 1 can kill the spine and admit Phases 0–1 are architecture-lock with a talk-path smoke test.

findings.criterion: nothing is spent, written, or started without a human confirmation
findings.section: Phase 10 pre-answering static gates; Phase 0 deferred pre-answering
findings.message: Steel-man pre-answering as a Phase-10 optimization: only hash-matched inventory gates, never the three Crucible approvals, off by default, opt-in per gate, layered on a proven resume channel. Any pre-answered gate is still a human gate that does not receive a human confirmation. The North Star’s confirmation law is not limited to spend and the three named Crucible approvals; it is “nothing… without a human confirmation.” The draft never reclassifies “static inventory gates” as non-decisions or machine-checkable preconditions. If they are real trio stops that change run trajectory, auto-answering them is a North Star breach even when steel-manned as “safe optimization.” Either drop pre-answering from this Master Plan (keep it deferred indefinitely), or amend the North Star to carve which gate classes may be pre-answered and still count as confirmed. Leaving it in Phase 10 as in-scope work reopens the silent-progress hole the whole confirm spine exists to close.

findings.criterion: project is stood up, planned, and driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD; plan change by talking; campaign ledger single source of truth
findings.section: Success criterion 1; Phase 6 draft-Face / zero-chat proof
findings.message: Steel-man E5: durable truth is Face + Strip receipts + roadmap events; dialogue is ephemeral compile input so the ledger stays clean. Amendment A1 already narrows talking to typed dialogue. Zero persisted turns then further reduces “talking to the steward” to: ephemeral UI turns that compile into draft-Face, then gate-confirm write, then later correction-as-commission. After reconnect, John only sees structured “what I have so far,” not the conversational thread that produced it. That can satisfy a storage purity goal while failing the product premise that the project is driven by talking to a steward — especially for corrections and mid-campaign direction, which become discrete propose→confirm transactions rather than ongoing dialogue. The North Star does not require transcript-as-SSOT, but it does require that talk is the control surface with continuity. The plan needs an explicit continuity model (what the steward can restate, what John can refer to, how “change by talking” cites prior talk) that is stronger than “draft state + commissions,” or it should admit the product is form-compile-plus-commissions with a chat skin.

findings.criterion: nothing spent/written/started without confirmation; propose for named step; say start → Foreman executes
findings.section: Phase 1 / Phase 3 confirm-count budget; Phase 10 re-measure
findings.message: Steel-man “at most two spend-confirms and five gate-confirms” as a design constraint that protects John from confirm fatigue while preserving required gates. Enumerate the North Star-required confirms on the full arc: Face first-write (gate), Crucible commission (spend), three Crucible approval gates (gates), plan correction path (spend or gate), typed start/Foreman commission (spend), plus budget-breach and lost-step re-confirms when they occur. Stand-up-to-artifact alone already pressures 1 spend + 4 gates before spare. The budget is defined and re-measured only on stand-up-to-artifact, not on stand-up-to-Foreman-truthful-Roadmap. Exceeding budget is a “design defect that reshapes the phase,” but the budget never accounts for the North Star’s last clause. Steel-manning the budget as UX discipline therefore either forces illegal removal of required confirms later, or the budget is a partial-path metric masquerading as a global constraint. Measure and budget the full North Star arc, or stop treating the partial budget as a falsifier of the whole grammar.

findings.criterion: NON-GOAL — no bespoke plan template (the Crucible plan shape IS the template)
findings.section: Phase 0 classifyArtifact falsification; Phase 8 artifact card
findings.message: Steel-man option (a): packaging a doc-trio so the existing classifier accepts it is “not a new template.” If classification fails on real Crucible outputs, a “manifest the classifier already understands” is still a presentation schema chosen because the native plan shape did not fit. That is how bespoke templates get born under a packaging label. Option (b) amendment gate is the honest path. The plan should require that option (a) only wraps files/paths the classifier already handles with zero new card fields or layout types; any new card field is automatically option (b). Without that bright line, Phase 0’s escape hatch can violate the non-goal while claiming to honor it.

findings.criterion: Anchor executes confirmed commission as a real trio run
findings.message: Steel-man “trio substrate” as job_runner/terminal_session/lanes without requiring researchPrime in v1. The draft’s real-execution proofs are Crucible HALT (Phase 5) and Foreman start (Phase 9). researchPrime appears only as something not to modify. If “trio run” in the North Star and success criteria includes researchPrime commissions, no phase proves propose→confirm→run→handback→artifact for that skill. If researchPrime is out of scope for this Master Plan, the success criteria and phase prose should say “Crucible and Foreman legs of the trio,” not “real trio run,” so the plan does not claim a three-skill product while proving two.

findings.criterion: n/a
findings.message: The reviser changelog is thirty identical “Applied a search/replace patch” lines. It does not state what claims changed relative to prior Shark findings. That does not refute the North Star directly, but it prevents steel-manning “this revision addressed X.” Process smell only; do not hold the loop open on this alone.

findings.criterion: Nothing is spent, written, or started without a human confirmation; Auth-ON proof (criterion 6)
findings.message: The plan hardens **tests** (`ANCHOR_TOKEN-set` is the default test mode; auth-off tests fail the wave) but never hardens **runtime**. It never states that boot or job entry **REFUSES** when the token is unset, empty, or the auth middleware is bypassed—only that outcomes must be proven with the token set. This surface “shipped broken twice… auth-off.” A suite that is green under auth-ON while production still starts and accepts unauthenticated starts is the same failure mode again: confirmation, `who`, and the choke point become optional furniture. Security requires a fail-closed production posture—no runner entry, no stream, no artifact fetch, no confirm endpoint without a verified principal—asserted by a negative boot/entry test, not by test-mode convention.

findings.criterion: confirmation records `who`; only John’s explicit confirmation; service must not confirm spend
findings.message: Tokens are bound to `(project_id, step_id, commission_hash, principal)` and “service may NOT confirm spend,” but the plan never specifies how principal is **derived and verified**. If `principal` is a client-supplied field, a header the UI invents, or anything other than a server-side binding from the credential that authenticated the request, an unauthenticated or service caller can mint or redeem a confirm as `john`. Then the ledger’s `who` is a label, not evidence, and the service ban is a comment. Refutation demand: principal MUST be server-resolved from the auth credential at mint and at CAS consume; client-asserted `who` is rejected; tests prove service credentials cannot produce a spend-confirm or gate-confirm ledger row under any payload.

findings.criterion: campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.message: Python has no write credential to `roadmap_events` (good) but **owns** an outbox the single Node writer drains into the authoritative ledger. The plan names content hash, `outbox_id` dedupe, and crash atomicity—none of which authenticate **who may assert** a status flip for a given `run_id`/`commission`. A buggy, compromised, or second local process that can append to that outbox can inject `complete` / wave-GREEN / false liveness that the drain will faithfully promote into SSOT. Then every honest-status and chain-id reconstruction test passes on **poisoned truth**. Missing: outbox records cryptographically (or capability-) bound to the confirmed commission/run (e.g. run-scoped secret minted only after confirm, verified at drain), plus a negative test that an outbox row without that binding is refused and never becomes a `roadmap_events` row.

findings.criterion: nothing runs until John confirms what was proposed (skill + seat + depth + bound step before spend)
findings.message: The token binds `commission_hash`, but the plan does not require the **proposal payload John saw** to be immutable and byte-identical to what the runner launches at consume. Without store-level immutability of the proposal after mint, re-hash on CAS that covers skill/seat/depth/step/ceiling/plan-hash/argv inputs, and a negative test that mutating the proposal after mint invalidates the token, John can confirm screen A while the supervisor enqueues screen B. Hash-of-something is not integrity if the something is still writable or the hash omits the spend-critical fields. This is the classic confirm-TOCTOU that voids “explicit confirmation” as a security control.

findings.criterion: nothing is started without a human confirmation; gate answers are micro-commissions on the same spine
findings.message: Halt records store `resume_token` alongside gate metadata. The plan requires signed confirmation records for gate **passage** and negative-tests zero-confirm runs reaching Stage-2, but it never states that **possessing or replaying `resume_token` alone cannot resume**. If the supervisor can `--resume` (or live-stdin inject) from a stored token without a consumed gate-confirm CAS row bound to that `gate_id` + `face_hash` + principal, the Phase-3 choke point is side-doored for the entire remaining paid run. Demand: resume is gated on a consumed confirmation id; resume_token is useless without it; negative test covers stolen halt-row / replayed resume_token.

findings.criterion: nothing started without confirmation; durable halt record is the spine (not terminal memory)
findings.section: Phase 5 — resume via checkpoint vs live-stdin fallback
findings.message: A live-stdin bridge “FALLBACK only if resume is measured lossy” is an unhardened second control plane. Stdin answers can bypass durable halt/confirm machinery, skip `who` recording, and invent gate satisfaction that never appears as a first-class ledger event—exactly the “auto-passed gate indistinguishable from approved” failure the phase claims to close. Either forbid live-stdin for any gate that advances spend, or put it behind the same single-use confirm token and ledger event as `--resume`, with a negative test that stdin without a confirmation record does not advance the run.

findings.criterion: Nothing is spent, written, or started without a human confirmation (in-run gate decisions advance paid work)
findings.message: After the spine is “proven,” Phase 10 layers pre-answering for inventory-hash-matched static gates (excluding the three Crucible approvals). That is still **auto-advancing a halted paid run without John**. Hash equality on rendered text is not a human confirmation; inventory incompleteness, dynamic interpolation, or a wrong static classification turns pre-answer into silent gate passage—the failure mode Phase 0’s unknown-halt rule was written to prevent. Off-by-default opt-in does not make it North-Star-safe; it makes the bypass optional. Either drop pre-answering from Stage-1 scope, or require each enablement to be a recorded gate-confirm of the **policy** (which gates, which answers) with the same `who`, and prove pre-answer cannot fire on any gate not on that signed allowlist.

findings.criterion: Auth-ON integrity of confirm path; nothing spent without John’s confirmation
findings.section: Phase 8 — reviewable artifact / raw doc-trio; Phase 3 — stream auth
findings.message: The plan stores and renders raw trio output and plan documents as first-class UI. It never names HTML/script sanitization, CSP, or non-HTML rendering for untrusted model/plan content. On a browser-hosted Anchor surface, a malicious or merely malformed plan can execute in the origin that holds `ANCHOR_TOKEN` / session credentials and drive propose→confirm or start paths as John. Auth-on-stream and “no token in query string” are irrelevant if the page itself is the attacker. Demand: untrusted artifact bytes render as text/sandbox; confirm actions require a separate anti-automation step not callable from injected script alone (or equivalent origin isolation), with an XSS-class negative test in the auth-ON suite.

findings.criterion: only John’s explicit confirmation starts spend
findings.section: Phase 3 — auth on stream and confirm endpoints
findings.message: Auth checks on SSE/frames and “no token in query string” are necessary but incomplete. The plan never specifies token transport (header vs cookie vs memory), CSRF defenses on state-changing confirm/start endpoints, or that a cross-site request cannot redeem a minted single-use confirmation id while John’s browser holds a session. Single-human / local-host does not eliminate browser CSRF. Without SameSite/CSRF-token/custom-header requirements and a negative cross-origin confirm test, “explicit confirmation” can be forged by any page John has open.

findings.criterion: nothing runs until confirmed; start-path inventory: inventoried-but-open bypass is a hole
findings.section: Phase 1 vs Phase 0 start-path inventory / Phase 3 negative tests
findings.message: Phase 0 correctly treats open start paths as holes. Phase 1’s green condition is a full motion auth-ON observed run, while “per-start-path negative tests” and delete/hard-disable of non-routable paths are **owed to Phase 3**. That ordering lets the “walking skeleton” declare North-Star motion while alternate entry symbols (UI buttons, HTTP routes, Node callers) still start work without the token. Phase 1 already claims real store, real token, real confirm—so it cannot defer closure of inventoried bypasses. Either Phase 1’s green includes “every Phase-0 path refuses unconfirmed start,” or Phase 1 must not claim the confirmation choke point is real.

findings.criterion: confirmation records `who`; gate passage is evidenced, not ambient
findings.message: “Signed confirmation record carrying real principal + gate_id + face_hash” never defines the signature system: HMAC key custody, what is covered, verification at resume, and failure mode on bad signature. Without that, “signed” is prose and any row in the confirmations table can satisfy the negative test that only checks for row presence. Security control requires verify-before-resume and a test that a tampered principal/gate_id/face_hash/answer fails closed.

findings.criterion: nothing is started without confirmation (only the confirmed commission starts)
findings.message: Blocking `--yes` / `--auto-approve` / `-y` prevents one class of unattended approval, not command/argument injection. Free-form paths, env, working directories, extra flags, or multi-arg smuggling can start a different engine, different project tree, or extra process that was never on the confirm screen. The allowlist must be a closed schema (enum flags + validated path roots bound to the confirmed project/plan hash), with adversarial fixtures beyond the three auto-approve strings, or “confirmed commission” does not equal “confirmed process image.”

findings.criterion: Nothing is … written … without a human confirmation (Face first write is called out; draft is not)
findings.section: Phase 6 — draft-Face; Success criterion 1 / North Star write clause
findings.message: The plan forbids silent Face persistence until gate-confirm, yet every framing turn appends an immutable draft revision without confirmation. If “written” includes durable project state John did not approve, draft-Face is a silent write channel (and a recovery surface for content John never confirmed). Either explicitly scope the North Star write clause to Face/commission/ledger spend artifacts (and record that draft is ephemeral/non-authoritative), or require a confirm boundary before draft leaves process memory. As written, the law and the mechanism disagree.

findings.criterion: nothing is spent … without a human confirmation
findings.message: “Zero-spend” is asserted by stubbing the trio, not by a hard spend-accounting control. If the stub path shares any live credential, network lane, or job_runner entry that can touch real seats, rehearsal is a confirmation-free spend probe. Demand a structural guarantee (no live driver credentials on rehearsal; runner rejects real backends when commission class=rehearsal) plus a test that rehearsal cannot produce billable side effects—not a naming convention.

findings.criterion: n/a
findings.message: Thirty lines of “Applied a search/replace patch” provide no security delta to re-verify. That is a process smell for this tank round, not a North Star defect; demote and do not hold the loop on it.

demoted.section: Process / last revision metadata (not a plan phase)
demoted.message: The reviser’s changelog is thirty identical “Applied a search/replace patch” lines. That does not refute a North Star criterion, but it does make future Shark/maintainer comparison of revisions impossible. Demote per inclusion test; fix process, not product scope.

The reviser changelog is thirty identical “Applied a search/replace patch” lines. It does not state what claims changed relative to prior Shark findings. That does not refute the North Star directly, but it prevents steel-manning “this revision addressed X.” Process smell only; do not hold the loop open on this alone.
Thirty lines of “Applied a search/replace patch” provide no security delta to re-verify. That is a process smell for this tank round, not a North Star defect; demote and do not hold the loop on it.

reviews.note: Skeptic Shark, future-maintainer angle only. Changelog is opaque (“search/replace” ×30) so revision intent cannot be audited; findings target the draft body as written.

findings.criterion: real trio run returns a validated handback; malformed/incomplete still leaves something to read; campaign ledger is single source of truth
findings.message: D-A locks a decision *rule* before measurement, then forks product law into three incompatible regimes (refuse on absent soft fields / degrade / strike-or-amend) depending on an extractability matrix that does not yet exist. A future maintainer—and Stage-2—cannot know which envelope is the product. The success criteria still list six required fields as if the strict envelope is settled. Until Stage-1 lock records the measured branch with `who` and rewrites criteria 3 / Phase 8 to a single non-forked acceptance law, this is not a locked design; it is a choose-your-own-handback plan that will be “implemented” three different ways under schedule pressure.

findings.criterion: nothing spent, written, or started without human confirmation; single writer proven; honest Roadmap status
findings.message: Phase 1 is allowed to ship the full talk→artifact motion without concurrency/crash receipts, CAS/idempotency/auth baseline, lease liveness, or real-Crucible HALT—while insisting those gates are “named and owed.” The debt lives only in paragraph lists. There is no machine-checkable owed-gate register, no Phase-10 gate that fails if any Phase-1 skip lacks a later receipt, and no rule that a later wave may not declare GREEN while an owed gate is still open. A future maintainer cannot tell done from deferred; schedule pressure will treat Phase-1 GREEN as the product. For a plan whose North Star is “no silent spend + ledger truth,” unenforced debt is a silent-exemption machine.

findings.criterion: project stood up, planned, and driven by talking to its steward (compile Face/Roadmap, propose named-step commission, typed refine, start→Foreman)
findings.message: The North Star product is “the steward.” The draft never draws a maintainable boundary: which modules own dialogue compile, draft-Face, propose/confirm surface, adapter, handback, Roadmap projection, and AWAITING YOU. Work is scattered across job-lifecycle line cites, packet-view, store writers, supervisor, and unnamed UI. A future maintainer will not know where “talk to the steward” lives, will re-implement conversation and confirm paths in new call sites, and will re-open the multi-writer / multi-confirm bypasses Phase 0–3 try to close. Without a seam map and “one owner per motion,” the talk path is institutional knowledge, not a system.

findings.topic: trio inventory drift has no re-inventory protocol
findings.criterion: nothing starts or proceeds without human confirmation; Roadmap shows the truth about what is waiting/running; non-goal forbids changing trio sources
findings.message: Gate inventory is a one-time Phase-0 table (verbatim text + sha256). Pre-answering is hash-exact; unknown halts show raw text. The plan never says who re-runs the inventory when Crucible/Foreman change gate wording, resume flags, or blocker shapes on *their* cadence (allowed by non-goal: you do not control them). A future maintainer inherits a frozen inventory that silently drifts into “everything is unknown halt” or, worse, stale pre-answer opt-ins that no longer match live engines. Without a versioned re-inventory trigger (trio version / binary hash / inventory age) and a test that fails when live halt text is neither inventoried nor routed as unknown, confirmation and honest wait-state rot by default.

findings.criterion: confirmed commission executes as a real trio/Foreman run; Roadmap truth across halt/resume/restart
findings.message: Phase 5 makes `--resume` primary and live-stdin a “fallback if resume is measured lossy,” then Phase 7 builds budget-breach resume on the same fork (resume suspended job object vs relaunch `--resume`, with honesty text if lossy). The measurement is deferred into the build. That freezes two execution topologies as forever-supported unless a later decision kills one. A future maintainer debugging “confirm said continue but the run re-billed / lost checkpoint / wrong wave state” has no single resume law—only a matrix of job-object + checkpoint + optional stdin bridge. Lock one resume contract (or a dated kill of the other) before Phases 5/7 both harden both paths.

findings.topic: rehearsal/stub CI vs real path bitrot
findings.criterion: Anchor executes a real trio run; when he says start, Foreman executes; Roadmap shows true state
findings.message: From Phase 1/4 onward, CI and continuous proof lean on a stub/rehearsal commission emitting canned doc-trio bytes. Real Crucible appears only as one observed HALT cycle (Phase 5); real Foreman only as one observed wave (Phase 9). There is no standing contract that rehearsal argv, halt shape, journal events, and handback extractors are re-diffed against live engines on a cadence. Future maintainers will keep green stub CI while the paid path drifts—exactly the failure mode that already burned auth-ON. A North Star that requires *real* execution needs a real-path canary that fails the suite when stub and live diverge, not a one-shot human observation per phase.

findings.criterion: steward proposes a commission for a named roadmap step (skill+seat+depth) without doing the planning itself
findings.message: The inverse guard depends on the proposer *declaring* whether it invented plan content. Models (and future prompt edits) will learn to under-report invention. That lets HOW leak into propose-time derivation while compile stays “WHAT/WHY-only,” violating the non-goal that the steward commissions rather than plans—and producing confidently wrong skill/seat/depth on the confirm screen. A future maintainer cannot audit the bright line without an external oracle (forbidden construct lint on propose inputs/outputs, fixture steps that must refuse, or human-labeled probe corpus). Self-attestation is not a maintainable guardrail.

findings.criterion: campaign ledger is single source of truth; Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.message: The plan admits the ledger *lags* between Python outbox append and Node drain, says the bound is “measured and recorded,” and forbids presenting undrained outbox as live status. It never defines an enforceable lag SLO, a surface that shows “as of seq N / lag exceeds bound,” or a failure when the drain stalls. A future maintainer inherits a system that can be “correct by design” while the Roadmap is minutes stale—or stuck—without failing any named gate. Honest status requires a numeric bound + test/alert, not a wave-receipt footnote.

findings.topic: Face / commission / handback schema evolution unspecified
findings.criterion: plan is an artifact John can change by talking; commissions pin Face hash; ledger remains SSOT
findings.message: Face versions are immutable and content-addressed; commissions pin Face hash; handbacks carry provenance. There is no migration/compat rule for when the Face step shape, draft-Face document, commission record, or handback envelope must change. A future maintainer either freezes schemas forever or ships breaking writers that leave old chain_id histories unreadable or unre-commissionable. Without versioned schemas + explicit read-compat tests (“old Face hash still resolves; old confirmation still reconstructs”), the ledger SSOT claim dies at the first enrichment the plan itself invites via “future decision-log entries.”

findings.criterion: full talk→Face→propose→confirm→run→artifact→honest status motion
findings.message: Phase 1 GREEN requires “one observed run of the full motion, by John, on the real machine.” That is a fine Stage-1 demo, not a maintainable regression gate. Future maintainers (and later waves) cannot re-prove the spine without the same human ritual, so the motion will silently regress between Phase 1 and Phase 10. Pair the human observation with an automatable auth-ON spine script that asserts the same chain_id-linked observables; otherwise the walking skeleton cannot walk after the author leaves the room.

findings.topic: brittle line-number cites as choke identity
findings.criterion: commission proposed and confirmed only through explicit human confirmation before spend
findings.message: The plan identifies the confirmation choke as `proposeCommission (141) / confirmCommission (250)`. Line numbers rot on the next edit; a future maintainer grepping the plan will trust the wrong symbols or invent a parallel entrypoint. Name stable module exports + a single-entrypoint invariant test (“all start paths call X”), not source coordinates.

findings.criterion: typed description produces Face/roadmap with zero chat turns persisted; ledger is Strip + roadmap events + Face narrative
findings.message: The plan allows structured append-only draft-Face state while banning dialogue turns, then defines the zero-chat proof as “scan every table/file/blob for any persisted dialogue turn.” It never defines the schema predicate that distinguishes allowed framing fields from forbidden transcript. A future maintainer will reintroduce near-transcript blobs under “structured state” and still pass a naive string scan—or fail the scan on legitimate draft text. Specify the allowed draft schema and scan against that whitelist.

findings.topic: DOC-TRIO MANIFEST packaging vs template creep
findings.criterion: no bespoke plan template; Crucible plan shape IS the template; reviewable artifact on screen
findings.message: If classifyArtifact fails, the only non-amendment path is a “DOC-TRIO MANIFEST” that packages bytes the classifier already understands. “Packaging” is undefined (file layout? synthetic metadata? rewritten headings?). A future maintainer under delivery pressure will grow the manifest into a second plan shape while claiming non-goal compliance. Bound the manifest to an explicit, testable contract (list of allowed transforms; golden bytes; forbid new sections/fields not present on disk).

findings.criterion: nothing spent or decided without human confirmation (budget must not remove required confirms)
findings.message: “≤2 spend-confirms and ≤5 gate-confirms for stand-up-to-artifact” is asserted, not derived from the North Star’s required confirms (Face first write + three Crucible approvals + spend, etc.). The “one spare” is unexplained. A future maintainer will either treat the numbers as sacred UX law or quietly raise them. Tie the budget to a named enumerate of required confirms so breaches diagnose missing/extra gates rather than vibes.

findings.section: Process / last revision metadata (not a plan phase)
findings.criterion: n/a
findings.message: The reviser’s changelog is thirty identical “Applied a search/replace patch” lines. That does not refute a North Star criterion, but it does make future Shark/maintainer comparison of revisions impossible. Demote per inclusion test; fix process, not product scope.

reviews.note: Contrarian Shark, steel-man-the-premise. Findings only where even the draft’s strongest reading fails a North Star criterion; infrastructure polish without NS linkage is omitted or demoted.

findings.topic: Phase-1 falsifies plumbing not value path
findings.criterion: steward proposes a commission for a named roadmap step and only on confirmation Anchor executes it as a real trio run; the produced plan comes back as an artifact John can read
findings.message: Steel-man the premise that “the whole North Star is ONE motion” and that an early end-to-end slice can kill or reshape the spine. Even granted, Phase 1 stubs the only leg that makes the motion the North Star: the real trio. The slice proves typed describe → Face → propose → confirm → stub → canned doc-trio → card → status. That is orchestration plumbing. It cannot falsify whether a confirmed commission against real Crucible yields a plan John can read and correct by talking, nor whether “nothing is spent without confirmation” still holds when the engine actually spends. The named falsifiers are almost all about compile, confirm-count, classifier, or status-without-supervisor — none is “real commission failed to produce a reviewable plan.” A green Phase 1 therefore over-claims ordering evidence: it can kill talk-surface shape, not the commission→plan premise the North Star is about. Either Phase 1 must include one real (even single-gate) Crucible hop, or the plan must stop saying Phase 1 can kill the spine of the North Star motion.

findings.criterion: when he says start, Foreman executes and the Roadmap shows the truth about what is running; plan comes back as artifact; nothing spent/written/started without confirmation
findings.message: Steel-man the phased inversion: prove HALT first, Foreman last, then auth-ON acceptance. The product sentence in the North Star is one arc: talk → Face/roadmap → commission → real plan → read/correct by talk → say start → Foreman runs → Roadmap tells the truth. No phase’s GREEN condition is that full arc. Phase 5 greens on one halt→confirm→resume “to the next gate,” not Stage-2 plan on screen. Phase 9 greens on typed start → one Foreman wave → wave state across restart, assuming an already-approved plan. Phase 10 runs per-criterion scenarios (1–5 and 8) in isolation, not one observed stand-up-through-Foreman chain with ledger chain_id reconstruction of that full spend. Confirm-count is re-measured only for “stand-up-to-artifact,” not stand-up-to-Foreman-running. Even the strongest reading of “eight criteria cover the North Star” fails: the North Star is a single continuous behavior, and the plan never requires one green observation of that continuous behavior. Without that, the plan can ship eight green checkboxes and still never have demonstrated the product.

findings.topic: One halt cycle under-proves multi-gate plan path
findings.criterion: produced plan comes back as an artifact John can read on screen; nothing is started without human confirmation
findings.message: Steel-man “HALT is the normal path; unattended completion is special.” Crucible’s design is three you-approve gates before a plan is an artifact. Proving one observed halt→ask→confirm→resume cycle only proves the resume channel for a single gate hop. It does not prove: durable halt records across three sequential gates, three gate-confirms each recording `who`, no silent auto-pass, and a final reviewable plan card. The negative test “zero confirmation records cannot reach Stage-2 output” is necessary but not sufficient as the phase GREEN — a run could still break on the second or third gate after Phase 5 is declared green. If HALT-first is the load-bearing inversion, GREEN must be the multi-gate path that actually yields the artifact the North Star promises, not “reaches the next gate.”

findings.section: Phase 0 D-C / D-C inverse guard; Phase 6 proposability probe
findings.criterion: NON-GOAL — nothing that makes the steward do the planning itself rather than commission it; steward compiles description into Face and Roadmap, then proposes a commission
findings.message: Steel-man D-C: compile emits only WHAT/WHY so the steward does not invent HOW; size/seat/depth appear only at propose-before-spend. The inverse guard then requires every step to be proposable (skill + seat + depth) from step text + Face alone, and on failure the compile must multi-turn ask John clarifying questions until proposability passes. That loop is interactive scoping and decomposition under a different name. It is not “commission planning” — it is the steward driving planning-quality content into the Face before any commission exists, exactly the non-goal the bright line claims to prevent. Steel-manning “clarifications are still WHAT/WHY” does not help: the North Star separates compile-from-description vs commission-a-named-step; an unbounded clarify-until-proposable dialogue is planning work performed by the steward. The plan needs a hard stop (max clarify turns, escalate to John choosing “commission research/framing” as an explicit step, or accept that some steps are not yet commissionable without calling that “planning”).

findings.topic: SSOT dualized by ledger lag and lease
findings.section: Phase 2 honest SSOT bound; Phase 4 lease liveness; Success criterion 5 and 7
findings.criterion: campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.message: Steel-man the outbox design: Python cannot write roadmap_events; Node drains; at-least-once with dedupe; projection says “as of seq N.” The draft itself then makes liveness come from the lease, “never from the outbox,” and forbids presenting un-drained outbox as live status. That is two sources of truth by construction: ledger for committed history, lease for “is it running.” Criterion 7 (“roadmap_events has exactly ONE writer… campaign ledger SSOT”) and criterion 5 (“Roadmap reflects ACTUAL state”) are only jointly true if the plan names the dual model and defines which surface is authoritative for which question. As written, “single source of truth” is prose that the same phase falsifies. Steel-man cannot rescue a title claim the body retracts; rename SSOT to “append-only event log + lease-derived liveness” and make criterion 5/7 acceptance assert both, or the Roadmap can be “honest” while the ledger is stale and still called SSOT.

findings.topic: Validated-handback criterion may be permanently degraded
findings.section: Phase 0 D-A and extractability matrix; Phase 8; Success criterion 3
findings.criterion: real trio run returns a plan John can read; no changes to Crucible/Foreman/researchPrime; campaign ledger remains truth
findings.message: Steel-man “extract, do not invent” and the non-goal of zero trio source changes. D-A pre-commits refusal/degraded/strike rules to measured absent-rates on fields the trio was never designed to emit. If the matrix shows high absence (likely for uncertainty_flags, tool_depth_why, human_wait), criterion 3’s happy path — receipt-validate accepts a full envelope — becomes rare or impossible without amending the non-goal or striking fields. The degraded path (raw doc-trio + partial card + REFUSED banner) satisfies “never invisible spend” but does not satisfy “validated handback” or a trusted ledger receipt of what the run meant. The plan has no success bar for happy-path handback rate, no Stage-1 decision of which fields are load-bearing for “plan as artifact” vs Strip metadata, and Phase 10 still asserts “a real trio run returns a handback that receipt-validate.mjs accepts” as if that were independent of D-A’s measurement. Steel-manning extraction without a defined “good enough for North Star” envelope leaves criterion 3 either silently always-degraded or a future amendment bomb mid-build.

findings.section: Phase 1 near-term specifics (real substrate, real writer)
findings.criterion: campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; nothing spent/written/started without confirmation
findings.message: Steel-man “skeleton first so failure can still kill or reshape the spine.” Phase 1 already mandates D-B’s store (local non-synced SQLite/WAL), the single Node writer, roadmap_events/commissions/confirmations/blob shapes, real token/confirm grammar, and ledger events. The only allowed stub is the trio leg. The falsifiers reshape Phase 6 (compile line), Phases 3/7 (confirm budget), Phase 8 timing (artifact), or Phase 4 timing (lease) — not the outbox/single-writer/SQLite premise. So the “kill the spine” claim is oversold: the architectural spine is locked before it is stress-tested by real spend, real multi-gate HALT, or real Foreman. Ordering evidence is only about talk/confirm UX, while the durability and confirmation choke points the North Star depends on are already chosen. Either Phase 1 must be allowed to reject D-B/outbox on evidence, or the plan must stop claiming Phase 1 can kill the spine and admit Phases 0–1 are architecture-lock with a talk-path smoke test.

findings.section: Phase 10 pre-answering static gates; Phase 0 deferred pre-answering
findings.criterion: nothing is spent, written, or started without a human confirmation
findings.message: Steel-man pre-answering as a Phase-10 optimization: only hash-matched inventory gates, never the three Crucible approvals, off by default, opt-in per gate, layered on a proven resume channel. Any pre-answered gate is still a human gate that does not receive a human confirmation. The North Star’s confirmation law is not limited to spend and the three named Crucible approvals; it is “nothing… without a human confirmation.” The draft never reclassifies “static inventory gates” as non-decisions or machine-checkable preconditions. If they are real trio stops that change run trajectory, auto-answering them is a North Star breach even when steel-manned as “safe optimization.” Either drop pre-answering from this Master Plan (keep it deferred indefinitely), or amend the North Star to carve which gate classes may be pre-answered and still count as confirmed. Leaving it in Phase 10 as in-scope work reopens the silent-progress hole the whole confirm spine exists to close.

findings.section: Success criterion 1; Phase 6 draft-Face / zero-chat proof
findings.criterion: project is stood up, planned, and driven BY TALKING TO ITS STEWARD; plan change by talking; campaign ledger single source of truth
findings.message: Steel-man E5: durable truth is Face + Strip receipts + roadmap events; dialogue is ephemeral compile input so the ledger stays clean. Amendment A1 already narrows talking to typed dialogue. Zero persisted turns then further reduces “talking to the steward” to: ephemeral UI turns that compile into draft-Face, then gate-confirm write, then later correction-as-commission. After reconnect, John only sees structured “what I have so far,” not the conversational thread that produced it. That can satisfy a storage purity goal while failing the product premise that the project is driven by talking to a steward — especially for corrections and mid-campaign direction, which become discrete propose→confirm transactions rather than ongoing dialogue. The North Star does not require transcript-as-SSOT, but it does require that talk is the control surface with continuity. The plan needs an explicit continuity model (what the steward can restate, what John can refer to, how “change by talking” cites prior talk) that is stronger than “draft state + commissions,” or it should admit the product is form-compile-plus-commissions with a chat skin.

findings.topic: Confirm budget ignores full North Star motion
findings.section: Phase 1 / Phase 3 confirm-count budget; Phase 10 re-measure
findings.criterion: nothing spent/written/started without confirmation; propose for named step; say start → Foreman executes
findings.message: Steel-man “at most two spend-confirms and five gate-confirms” as a design constraint that protects John from confirm fatigue while preserving required gates. Enumerate the North Star-required confirms on the full arc: Face first-write (gate), Crucible commission (spend), three Crucible approval gates (gates), plan correction path (spend or gate), typed start/Foreman commission (spend), plus budget-breach and lost-step re-confirms when they occur. Stand-up-to-artifact alone already pressures 1 spend + 4 gates before spare. The budget is defined and re-measured only on stand-up-to-artifact, not on stand-up-to-Foreman-truthful-Roadmap. Exceeding budget is a “design defect that reshapes the phase,” but the budget never accounts for the North Star’s last clause. Steel-manning the budget as UX discipline therefore either forces illegal removal of required confirms later, or the budget is a partial-path metric masquerading as a global constraint. Measure and budget the full North Star arc, or stop treating the partial budget as a falsifier of the whole grammar.

findings.topic: DOC-TRIO MANIFEST as template smuggle risk
findings.section: Phase 0 classifyArtifact falsification; Phase 8 artifact card
findings.criterion: NON-GOAL — no bespoke plan template (the Crucible plan shape IS the template)
findings.message: Steel-man option (a): packaging a doc-trio so the existing classifier accepts it is “not a new template.” If classification fails on real Crucible outputs, a “manifest the classifier already understands” is still a presentation schema chosen because the native plan shape did not fit. That is how bespoke templates get born under a packaging label. Option (b) amendment gate is the honest path. The plan should require that option (a) only wraps files/paths the classifier already handles with zero new card fields or layout types; any new card field is automatically option (b). Without that bright line, Phase 0’s escape hatch can violate the non-goal while claiming to honor it.

findings.criterion: Anchor executes confirmed commission as a real trio run
findings.message: Steel-man “trio substrate” as job_runner/terminal_session/lanes without requiring researchPrime in v1. The draft’s real-execution proofs are Crucible HALT (Phase 5) and Foreman start (Phase 9). researchPrime appears only as something not to modify. If “trio run” in the North Star and success criteria includes researchPrime commissions, no phase proves propose→confirm→run→handback→artifact for that skill. If researchPrime is out of scope for this Master Plan, the success criteria and phase prose should say “Crucible and Foreman legs of the trio,” not “real trio run,” so the plan does not claim a three-skill product while proving two.

findings.criterion: n/a
findings.message: The reviser changelog is thirty identical “Applied a search/replace patch” lines. It does not state what claims changed relative to prior Shark findings. That does not refute the North Star directly, but it prevents steel-manning “this revision addressed X.” Process smell only; do not hold the loop open on this alone.

reviews.note: Analyst Shark, security angle only. Findings judged against the North Star’s confirmation, `who`, SSOT, and auth-ON criteria. Process noise in the reviser changelog is noted once and not inflated.

findings.criterion: Nothing is spent, written, or started without a human confirmation; Auth-ON proof (criterion 6)
findings.message: The plan hardens **tests** (`ANCHOR_TOKEN-set` is the default test mode; auth-off tests fail the wave) but never hardens **runtime**. It never states that boot or job entry **REFUSES** when the token is unset, empty, or the auth middleware is bypassed—only that outcomes must be proven with the token set. This surface “shipped broken twice… auth-off.” A suite that is green under auth-ON while production still starts and accepts unauthenticated starts is the same failure mode again: confirmation, `who`, and the choke point become optional furniture. Security requires a fail-closed production posture—no runner entry, no stream, no artifact fetch, no confirm endpoint without a verified principal—asserted by a negative boot/entry test, not by test-mode convention.

findings.criterion: confirmation records `who`; only John’s explicit confirmation; service must not confirm spend
findings.message: Tokens are bound to `(project_id, step_id, commission_hash, principal)` and “service may NOT confirm spend,” but the plan never specifies how principal is **derived and verified**. If `principal` is a client-supplied field, a header the UI invents, or anything other than a server-side binding from the credential that authenticated the request, an unauthenticated or service caller can mint or redeem a confirm as `john`. Then the ledger’s `who` is a label, not evidence, and the service ban is a comment. Refutation demand: principal MUST be server-resolved from the auth credential at mint and at CAS consume; client-asserted `who` is rejected; tests prove service credentials cannot produce a spend-confirm or gate-confirm ledger row under any payload.

findings.criterion: campaign ledger remains the single source of truth; Roadmap shows the truth about what is running
findings.message: Python has no write credential to `roadmap_events` (good) but **owns** an outbox the single Node writer drains into the authoritative ledger. The plan names content hash, `outbox_id` dedupe, and crash atomicity—none of which authenticate **who may assert** a status flip for a given `run_id`/`commission`. A buggy, compromised, or second local process that can append to that outbox can inject `complete` / wave-GREEN / false liveness that the drain will faithfully promote into SSOT. Then every honest-status and chain-id reconstruction test passes on **poisoned truth**. Missing: outbox records cryptographically (or capability-) bound to the confirmed commission/run (e.g. run-scoped secret minted only after confirm, verified at drain), plus a negative test that an outbox row without that binding is refused and never becomes a `roadmap_events` row.

findings.criterion: nothing runs until John confirms what was proposed (skill + seat + depth + bound step before spend)
findings.message: The token binds `commission_hash`, but the plan does not require the **proposal payload John saw** to be immutable and byte-identical to what the runner launches at consume. Without store-level immutability of the proposal after mint, re-hash on CAS that covers skill/seat/depth/step/ceiling/plan-hash/argv inputs, and a negative test that mutating the proposal after mint invalidates the token, John can confirm screen A while the supervisor enqueues screen B. Hash-of-something is not integrity if the something is still writable or the hash omits the spend-critical fields. This is the classic confirm-TOCTOU that voids “explicit confirmation” as a security control.

findings.criterion: nothing is started without a human confirmation; gate answers are micro-commissions on the same spine
findings.message: Halt records store `resume_token` alongside gate metadata. The plan requires signed confirmation records for gate **passage** and negative-tests zero-confirm runs reaching Stage-2, but it never states that **possessing or replaying `resume_token` alone cannot resume**. If the supervisor can `--resume` (or live-stdin inject) from a stored token without a consumed gate-confirm CAS row bound to that `gate_id` + `face_hash` + principal, the Phase-3 choke point is side-doored for the entire remaining paid run. Demand: resume is gated on a consumed confirmation id; resume_token is useless without it; negative test covers stolen halt-row / replayed resume_token.

findings.section: Phase 5 — resume via checkpoint vs live-stdin fallback
findings.criterion: nothing started without confirmation; durable halt record is the spine (not terminal memory)
findings.message: A live-stdin bridge “FALLBACK only if resume is measured lossy” is an unhardened second control plane. Stdin answers can bypass durable halt/confirm machinery, skip `who` recording, and invent gate satisfaction that never appears as a first-class ledger event—exactly the “auto-passed gate indistinguishable from approved” failure the phase claims to close. Either forbid live-stdin for any gate that advances spend, or put it behind the same single-use confirm token and ledger event as `--resume`, with a negative test that stdin without a confirmation record does not advance the run.

findings.criterion: Nothing is spent, written, or started without a human confirmation (in-run gate decisions advance paid work)
findings.message: After the spine is “proven,” Phase 10 layers pre-answering for inventory-hash-matched static gates (excluding the three Crucible approvals). That is still **auto-advancing a halted paid run without John**. Hash equality on rendered text is not a human confirmation; inventory incompleteness, dynamic interpolation, or a wrong static classification turns pre-answer into silent gate passage—the failure mode Phase 0’s unknown-halt rule was written to prevent. Off-by-default opt-in does not make it North-Star-safe; it makes the bypass optional. Either drop pre-answering from Stage-1 scope, or require each enablement to be a recorded gate-confirm of the **policy** (which gates, which answers) with the same `who`, and prove pre-answer cannot fire on any gate not on that signed allowlist.

findings.section: Phase 8 — reviewable artifact / raw doc-trio; Phase 3 — stream auth
findings.criterion: Auth-ON integrity of confirm path; nothing spent without John’s confirmation
findings.message: The plan stores and renders raw trio output and plan documents as first-class UI. It never names HTML/script sanitization, CSP, or non-HTML rendering for untrusted model/plan content. On a browser-hosted Anchor surface, a malicious or merely malformed plan can execute in the origin that holds `ANCHOR_TOKEN` / session credentials and drive propose→confirm or start paths as John. Auth-on-stream and “no token in query string” are irrelevant if the page itself is the attacker. Demand: untrusted artifact bytes render as text/sandbox; confirm actions require a separate anti-automation step not callable from injected script alone (or equivalent origin isolation), with an XSS-class negative test in the auth-ON suite.

findings.section: Phase 3 — auth on stream and confirm endpoints
findings.criterion: only John’s explicit confirmation starts spend
findings.message: Auth checks on SSE/frames and “no token in query string” are necessary but incomplete. The plan never specifies token transport (header vs cookie vs memory), CSRF defenses on state-changing confirm/start endpoints, or that a cross-site request cannot redeem a minted single-use confirmation id while John’s browser holds a session. Single-human / local-host does not eliminate browser CSRF. Without SameSite/CSRF-token/custom-header requirements and a negative cross-origin confirm test, “explicit confirmation” can be forged by any page John has open.

findings.topic: skeleton ships with open start paths
findings.section: Phase 1 vs Phase 0 start-path inventory / Phase 3 negative tests
findings.criterion: nothing runs until confirmed; start-path inventory: inventoried-but-open bypass is a hole
findings.message: Phase 0 correctly treats open start paths as holes. Phase 1’s green condition is a full motion auth-ON observed run, while “per-start-path negative tests” and delete/hard-disable of non-routable paths are **owed to Phase 3**. That ordering lets the “walking skeleton” declare North-Star motion while alternate entry symbols (UI buttons, HTTP routes, Node callers) still start work without the token. Phase 1 already claims real store, real token, real confirm—so it cannot defer closure of inventoried bypasses. Either Phase 1’s green includes “every Phase-0 path refuses unconfirmed start,” or Phase 1 must not claim the confirmation choke point is real.

findings.criterion: confirmation records `who`; gate passage is evidenced, not ambient
findings.message: “Signed confirmation record carrying real principal + gate_id + face_hash” never defines the signature system: HMAC key custody, what is covered, verification at resume, and failure mode on bad signature. Without that, “signed” is prose and any row in the confirmations table can satisfy the negative test that only checks for row presence. Security control requires verify-before-resume and a test that a tampered principal/gate_id/face_hash/answer fails closed.

findings.criterion: nothing is started without confirmation (only the confirmed commission starts)
findings.message: Blocking `--yes` / `--auto-approve` / `-y` prevents one class of unattended approval, not command/argument injection. Free-form paths, env, working directories, extra flags, or multi-arg smuggling can start a different engine, different project tree, or extra process that was never on the confirm screen. The allowlist must be a closed schema (enum flags + validated path roots bound to the confirmed project/plan hash), with adversarial fixtures beyond the three auto-approve strings, or “confirmed commission” does not equal “confirmed process image.”

findings.section: Phase 6 — draft-Face; Success criterion 1 / North Star write clause
findings.criterion: Nothing is … written … without a human confirmation (Face first write is called out; draft is not)
findings.message: The plan forbids silent Face persistence until gate-confirm, yet every framing turn appends an immutable draft revision without confirmation. If “written” includes durable project state John did not approve, draft-Face is a silent write channel (and a recovery surface for content John never confirmed). Either explicitly scope the North Star write clause to Face/commission/ledger spend artifacts (and record that draft is ephemeral/non-authoritative), or require a confirm boundary before draft leaves process memory. As written, the law and the mechanism disagree.

findings.criterion: nothing is spent … without a human confirmation
findings.message: “Zero-spend” is asserted by stubbing the trio, not by a hard spend-accounting control. If the stub path shares any live credential, network lane, or job_runner entry that can touch real seats, rehearsal is a confirmation-free spend probe. Demand a structural guarantee (no live driver credentials on rehearsal; runner rejects real backends when commission class=rehearsal) plus a test that rehearsal cannot produce billable side effects—not a naming convention.

findings.criterion: n/a
findings.message: Thirty lines of “Applied a search/replace patch” provide no security delta to re-verify. That is a process smell for this tank round, not a North Star defect; demote and do not hold the loop on it.
